title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Struck & Assayed. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll. Light theme and smooth motion are pinned by your brief and hold in every option.

options.label: Struck & Assayed
options.lineage: hallmarks and assay marks struck into finished metal
options.thesis: A hallmark answers exactly the question this site has to answer: who made this, where, and in what year. The page becomes a bright milled plate carrying struck marks, and refuses the dev-agency arrangement of dark hero plus three icon cards.
options.viewport: No hero card. The whole first screen is one continuous pale plate. The headline is struck into it at large scale with a real impressed edge, and a single row of small marks sits beneath it like a hallmark strip: a maker's mark, a date letter reading 2017, and a chartreuse-inked assay mark that is the primary action. Both audiences read the same strip and take different marks.
options.risk: Struck depth has to be earned with layered inset shadow, not a bevel filter. Executed thinly it flattens into ordinary light-grey minimalism.

raised.raise: The 24-template catalog is now one sweepable row of identical struck plates with a single varying mark, read across at a glance, instead of 24 independent cards.
Every mark sits on a visible registration grid with orthogonal rules connecting it, so nothing floats in unearned whitespace.
Display type reaches genuinely large scale and one field floods full-bleed, rather than everything sitting politely inside a container.
The page ground is one continuous plate rather than a stack of alternating section backgrounds.
Real emptiness is held at the centre of key compositions instead of every cell being filled.
Motion leaves a brief decaying trace rather than snapping, so movement reads as continuous.

options.label: The Practice Plate
options.lineage: the engraved nameplate and stationery beside a professional's door
options.thesis: Every buyer in the template audience already owns one of these: the engraved plate that says the practice is real and established. The site becomes that plate and its letterhead.
options.viewport: A tall engraved plate centred on warm paper, the practice name and founding year cut into it, services set as an engraved index below.
options.risk: This topped my own ranking, which is the problem: warm paper plus brass plus an engraved serif is very close to the look most models ship for any premium or established brief. Familiar and effective, but the least distinctive card on the table.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.lineage: the row of ballistic needles across a recording desk
options.thesis: Services and templates as a long row of identical instruments read by sweeping the whole bridge, never by opening one.
options.viewport: A full-width bridge of identical meter faces, each channel a capability, the row leaning together on load.
options.risk: Holds product clarity for the catalog's sweep-the-row behaviour, but loses audience identification: a dental practice does not read itself in a recording desk, and a needle is a poor carrier for what a template actually looks like.

options.label: Man-Machine Diagram
options.lineage: neon line diagrams on a strict traffic grid
options.thesis: Capabilities wired as a lit connector network.
options.viewport: A wiring schematic of the studio's capabilities, current travelling the connectors.
options.risk: Declined: neon on black fights the pinned light theme, and neither audience reads itself in it. Kept its connector logic.

options.label: Rebel Menu
options.lineage: torn-paper collage menus in scarlet, black and white
options.thesis: The catalog as full-frame poster splashes.
options.viewport: A scarlet field with template choices as jagged cutouts at reckless angles.
options.risk: Declined: a law firm will not buy from a punk poster, and reckless angles wreck a 24-item scan. Kept its nerve about scale.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.lineage: the full-bleed GPU scene of an experiential studio
options.thesis: A living shader ground with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: A breathing full-screen shader behind a single oversized word.
options.risk: Declined: it sells an experiential studio, which misrepresents a practical services practice, hides the offer, and is heavy for a free-tier static host. Kept its single continuous surface.

options.label: Accretion Disk
options.lineage: a black-hole disk at the edge of disappearance
options.thesis: Navigation as orbital viewpoints around an unmarked centre.
options.viewport: A warped luminous disk with labels orbiting the rim.
options.risk: Declined on both axes: a services page is not an astrophysics viewer. Kept its unmarked centre.

options.label: Plankton Wake
options.lineage: a night sea igniting under motion
options.thesis: Pointer trails lighting a dark field.
options.viewport: A dark field where movement draws decaying light.
options.risk: Declined: a dark sea fights the pinned light theme and neither audience identifies with it. Kept its decaying-trace motion.

canonCard.label: The Category Standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category actually ships: a large centred headline, a soft gradient or subtle mesh, a logo strip, three-to-four capability cards, a process row, testimonials, a closing CTA.
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline, subhead, two buttons, product or abstract visual beneath, trust logos under the fold.
canonCard.risk: Instantly legible to both audiences and completely forgettable. Your buyers have six of these open in other tabs.
